routes.label: Combine the products into one cosine

question: If \(\sin2x\sin3x=\cos2x\cos3x,\) then one value for \(x\) is
solution:
The equality will hold if \(2x\) and \(3x\) are complementary acute angles: the sine of each will equal the cosine of the other. Set
\[
2x+3x=90^\circ,
\]
which gives \(x=18^\circ\).

For this value, the two angles are \(36^\circ\) and \(54^\circ\), and
\[
\sin36^\circ=\cos54^\circ,
\qquad
\sin54^\circ=\cos36^\circ.
\]
Multiplying these identities verifies the original equation. Therefore one value is \(\boxed{18^\circ}\), choice A.

solutionMethods.explanation:
The two products are the terms in the cosine addition formula
\[
\cos(A+B)=\cos A\cos B-\sin A\sin B.
\]
Moving the sine product to the other side of the given equation therefore gives
\[
0=\cos2x\cos3x-\sin2x\sin3x=\cos5x.
\]
Since \(\cos90^\circ=0\), choosing \(5x=90^\circ\) makes the equation true. Thus one value is \(\boxed{18^\circ}\), choice A.
